# `start_track_object`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start tracking an object inside a user-supplied rectangle on the live image.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdbbf0, StartObjTrack @0x3dd560 (64-bit build); firmware 9.75 handler @0xef280, relay check @0xbc980, smart-follow submit @0x4711e0 |

Object params with integer x, y, width and height. The request may first be forwarded to the other process (relay checks run before local validation). Locally it requires view mode 1 or the wide camera selected, the RTSP stream running, an existing tracker and a usable camera subframe; the RTMP setting must be zero. It initialises the tracker with the rectangle and centre and launches an object-tracking thread. The reply acknowledges the launch, not any tracking result. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: while smart follow runs, the rectangle is passed to the smart-follow worker instead; the rectangle is corrected when is_manual_selection is false and the tracker takes more arguments; error 106 is new. If smart follow runs, a rejected submit replies 209 (nonpositive width or height), 524 (worker stopped) or 268 (target pending or stage not accepting one); the subframe fallback does not apply there (firmware 9.75, both builds, READ). is_manual_selection (64-bit only) accepts JSON booleans and integers, other types give 106. Before the relay check, in a dual-camera main process the handler probes the other process with is_func_work for SmartFollow and ObjectTrack (10000 ms each). The relay check gives 203 (mount occupied) or 524 (AviRecord or MotionMonitor working). Firmware 9.75 32-bit: reads only the four integer coordinates (104), uses the older conversions, does not read is_manual_selection, and routes to smart-follow submission or ordinary tracking as on 64-bit (READ).

Side effects: Initialises the tracker region of interest and centre and starts an object-tracking worker thread. Forwarded requests have a delegated wait of 10000 ms, which is not a whole-call deadline. No explicit RPC timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_track_object"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Object required. All four members are required integers; no range check is applied by the handler. Integer-tag values use signed 32-bit storage. The rectangle is INFERRED to be in displayed-image pixel coordinates; the device converts all four through its display-to-sensor mapping, which depends on display and read-AVI state. [READ] |
| `params.x` | integer | yes | - | Rectangle left edge, displayed-image pixels (INFERRED). Missing, null or non-integer is rejected with 104. [READ] |
| `params.y` | integer | yes | - | Rectangle top edge, displayed-image pixels (INFERRED). Missing, null or non-integer is rejected with 104. [READ] |
| `params.width` | integer | yes | - | Rectangle width. If the converted width or height is 0 or negative, the device substitutes the camera subframe instead of rejecting the request. [READ] |
| `params.height` | integer | yes | - | Rectangle height. See width. [READ] |
| `params.is_manual_selection` | boolean | no | - | Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: optional bool, default true. Wrong type 106. When false, the rectangle is passed through a correction step before use (a change is logged); the 9.31 conversion is replaced by a show-to-sensor conversion in both cases. Absent from the 32-bit build. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | params absent or not an object, or any of x, y, width, height missing, null or not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 300 | View mode or camera not allowed, tracker missing, RTSP not running, camera subframe unavailable, RTMP setting active, or forwarding context null | `internal error` |
| 268 | A competing tracking worker is running | `operation is in progress` |
| 203 | Relay occupancy check finds the local or other-process mount occupied | `equipment is moving` |
| 212 | The tracking thread could not be created | `fail to create thread` |
| 524 | Firmware 9.75: AviRecord or MotionMonitor works locally or in the other process | `function conflict` |
| 106 | Firmware 9.75: is_manual_selection is not a bool | `expected bool` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Tracker virtual-call failures and relay or waiter failures are propagated and unresolved. The list is not claimed exhaustive.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":110,"method":"start_track_object","params":{"x":400,"y":300,"width":120,"height":120}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"method":"start_track_object","result":0,"code":0,"id":110}
```

Reply, bad-rectangle:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_track_object","error":"expected int param","code":104,"id":111}
```
